response.sql:
WITH matched_labs AS (
    SELECT p.ID, p.SEX, l.PT, l.IGA, l.IGM
    FROM Laboratory AS l
    JOIN Patient AS p ON p.ID = l.ID
), patient_avgs AS (
    SELECT ID, SEX,
           AVG(PT) AS avg_pt,
           AVG(IGA - IGM) AS avg_iga_minus_igm
    FROM matched_labs
    GROUP BY ID, SEX
), patient_ratios AS (
    SELECT ID, SEX, avg_pt, avg_iga_minus_igm,
           avg_iga_minus_igm / NULLIF(AVG(avg_iga_minus_igm) OVER (), 0) AS ratio_to_overall_mean
    FROM patient_avgs
)
SELECT SEX,
       AVG(avg_pt) AS avg_pt,
       AVG(avg_iga_minus_igm) AS avg_iga_minus_igm,
       AVG(ratio_to_overall_mean) AS avg_ratio_to_overall_mean
FROM patient_ratios
GROUP BY SEX;

assumptions.assumption: The sex breakdown averages each patient's per-patient averages and ratio equally, so patients with more laboratory records do not receive extra weight.

alternatives.interpretation: If each sex's averages should instead pool all matched laboratory records, weighting patients by their number of records, while the ratio remains the average of patient-level ratios:
alternatives.sql:
WITH matched_labs AS (
    SELECT p.ID, p.SEX, l.PT, l.IGA, l.IGM
    FROM Laboratory AS l
    JOIN Patient AS p ON p.ID = l.ID
), patient_avgs AS (
    SELECT ID, SEX, AVG(IGA - IGM) AS avg_iga_minus_igm
    FROM matched_labs
    GROUP BY ID, SEX
), overall_mean AS (
    SELECT AVG(avg_iga_minus_igm) AS mean_iga_minus_igm
    FROM patient_avgs
), patient_ratios AS (
    SELECT ID, SEX,
           avg_iga_minus_igm / NULLIF(mean_iga_minus_igm, 0) AS ratio_to_overall_mean
    FROM patient_avgs CROSS JOIN overall_mean
)
SELECT m.SEX,
       AVG(m.PT) AS avg_pt,
       AVG(m.IGA - m.IGM) AS avg_iga_minus_igm,
       AVG(r.ratio_to_overall_mean) AS avg_ratio_to_overall_mean
FROM matched_labs AS m
JOIN patient_ratios AS r ON r.ID = m.ID AND r.SEX = m.SEX
GROUP BY m.SEX;
